fatal_errors: The proposed material is homogenized equiatomic AlCoCrFeNi, whereas the target is as-cast, non-equiatomic AlCoCrFeNi2.1 with a specific L12/B2 eutectic lamellar microstructure.

The hypothesis treats 600–800 °C as the tribo-corrosion service temperature. The target sliding tests were conducted in deionized water at 25–100 °C; approximately 1100 °C was used only for brief thermal-shock cycles.
A salt solution at 700 °C is not a physically coherent conventional aqueous tribo-corrosion condition without specifying a pressurized or molten-salt apparatus.
The proposed oxidizing-atmosphere oxide-scale mechanism replaces the target competition among aqueous passivation, sliding-induced depassivation, repassivation, and tribo-layer disruption.
The comparator is left generic rather than identifying identically conditioned duplex stainless steel 2205.
explanation: The response captures only the broad direction that an Al-Co-Cr-Fe-Ni HEA may outperform stainless steel in tribo-corrosion. It does not reconstruct the actual alloy composition, as-cast lamellar dual-phase state, DS2205 comparator, immersed deionized-water conditions, or the nonmonotonic temperature response with minimum degradation near 50 °C. Its generic protective-oxide and slow-diffusion explanation has limited overlap with the observed passivation and tribo-layer mechanism and is unsupported by evidence. Although the comparative experiment has a nominal falsification rule, its proposed 700 °C salt-solution condition is ill-defined and would test a substantially different materials problem.
